notes: Lengths and translations are metres, time seconds, angles degrees, colours sRGB hex. Height is nominal standing height, including prone and seated rigs, not their posed bounding box.
Figure +X is its left, +Y up, +Z forward. Map east is +X, north -Z. Convert map coordinates to [2000*(x-500), elevation, 2000*(y-770)] before display exaggeration.

Part transform = parent joint * translation(at + animation position) * rotationXYZ(rest + animation rotation). Translate the primitive by centre afterward; child joints must not inherit centre or geometry scaling. Root channels transform the entire rig about figure origin.

Capsule length includes its caps. Use x diameter for cap height; z is its transverse scale. Do not extend caps beyond the stated full length. Lower leg ends include the foot silhouette; hands are included in forearms.
Channels evaluate offset + amplitude*sin(2*pi*(harmonic*t+phase)); absent channels are zero. Offsets add to rest rotations. Negative shoulder rx reaches forward and up.

One stride is two steps. Drive walk and run t by distance/stride after undoing display scale. Their periods are reference cadence only. Run uses the same stride at higher cadence. Root motion does not add to path distance.
Sine gaits approximate foot contact rather than solving planted-foot IK. Optional stance locking may reduce sliding at close range; do not stretch limbs or sink a body to lock both feet.
Use independent phases for Pure Titans and civilians, smaller phase differences along the Wall Titan front. Freeze locomotion when stopped. Follow existing night inactivity and reduced-motion state.

Horse attach.saddle is figure-space at rest, on the saddle top; carry it with the animated body joint. Align rider torso pivot [0,0.58,0] to this point. Rider origin is feet-grounded for inspection, not the seat. Match horse and rider walk phase and stride; apply rider bob relative to mount once.

Boat and steamer origins are hull bottoms: place boat -0.35 m and steamer -1.7 m relative to water. Pier origin is foundation; deck top is 3.25 m above it. Props face +Z. Cannon local barrel +Y points toward muzzle; fire runs once t=0..1 then returns to rest.

Use shared primitives with 6-8 radial segments and 4-6 sphere latitude bands. Smooth flesh, flat foliage and stone. Standard roughness 0.9, metalness 0; cannon and rails roughness 0.65, metalness 0.15. Avoid outlines and separate eye meshes.
Rotated boxes make diamond-section gabled roofs; lower halves sit inside the building. Palace and chapel roof cones may use four radial segments. Stump includes a broken base and a fallen trunk.

Terrain heights are art ranges above sea level, not surveyed geography. Blend class boundaries, flatten town foundations and gate approaches, and seat walls, tracks and figures on the same surface. Keep waterways continuous.

Normalize sunDir: it points toward the light. Day sun is northwest, approximately 29 degrees above horizon. Choose fog start/end after exaggeration so all three Walls remain readable. Use emissive window faces rather than individual point lights.

FX dimensions are metres; life, period, interval and fade are seconds; speed is m/s. waveSpeed is cycles/s and waveHeight peak amplitude. Size is diameter, endSize final diameter; cloud width and length are full extents. Spawn dust at foot contact, flares only at story signals.

Pool a few low-poly transparent steam puffs; use broad vertex-alpha cloud shadow patches. Avoid full-island transparent layers and thousands of shadow casters. Town lights only appear where people still live.

Pitch means depression below horizontal, not polar angle from +Y. Camera sits south of focus with north at the top; blend target and pitch smoothly. Exaggeration belongs to the scene; retain Wall-to-Wall-Titan 50:60 and adult-to-child ratios when sharing a view.

Wall Titans are 60 m but exposed masonry is 50 m: conceal their lower 10 m when embedded and lift their origin to ground on release. Do not shorten rigs, show heads over intact Walls or expose them before the story reveal.

Figures use integral hands and feet to stay inside the part budgets. Civilian legs, horse legs and the seated rider each use one primitive per limb; rider legs angle forward under the saddle. These are deliberate crowd silhouettes, not close-up anatomical rigs.
